title: STRATA
subtitle: An excavation through the deep history of the pantheons — from the first Dreaming to the mythic geography of the modern map.
note: Chronology orders by continuity depth: unbroken oral traditions rank by the age of their continuity; literate traditions by earliest attestation, with oral layers noted. Dating follows mainstream scholarship; contested dates carry their uncertainty in the open.

layers.name: The Dreamtime
layers.attestation: The oldest continuous tradition on Earth: carried unbroken since the first settlement of Sahul, long before writing existed anywhere.
layers.scriptNote: No writing — the archive is the land itself: songlines, rock art, ceremony.
survivals: Songlines still walked today
the place-names of an entire continent
rock art tens of millennia deep
layers.material: ochre bedrock — the deepest layer, the foundation stone
layers.summary: Every other stratum in this excavation was buried and forgotten and dug up again. The Dreamtime was never buried. Its beings did not pass into myth — they remained in practice, the longest unbroken act of remembrance our species performs.

layers.name: The First Writing
layers.attestation: The first attested pantheon anywhere: Sumerian theonyms appear in cuneiform by the Early Dynastic period; Akkadian, Babylonian and Assyrian hands continue the same gods for two and a half millennia.
layers.scriptNote: Cuneiform — the script that taught the world to write: 𒀭 dingir, the divine determinative, marks every name of a god.
survivals: the seven-day week
the 60-minute hour
the flood narrative the Hebrew Bible inherits
epic itself — Gilgameš is the first hero
layers.material: fired river silt — the first tablets
layers.summary: Here the gods first learned to be written down. Enki's me — the divine decrees of civilization — is humanity's first theory of what a god is for: the custody of the arts, one by one.

layers.name: The Everlasting
layers.attestation: Three thousand years of continuous state cult — the Pyramid Texts (c. 2350 BCE) are the world's oldest large religious corpus, still legible to the last Egyptian temples.
layers.scriptNote: Hieroglyphs — 𓇋𓏏𓆑 for Thoth, 𓂀 the Eye — a writing system that kept its sacred character for three millennia.
survivals: Isis worshipped across the entire Roman Empire
the obelisk on every piazza
the Book of the Dead as world literature
layers.summary: The Egyptian answer to death was the most confident ever built: not an end but a change of address. Osiris dies and rules the dead — the first god whose resurrection is the guarantee of every follower's own.

layers.name: The Vedic Current
layers.attestation: The Rigveda was composed c. 1500–1200 BCE and transmitted orally, syllable-perfect, for three millennia before fixation — the oldest religious text still in living use. The Indus inheritance beneath it is older still, and still unread.
layers.scriptNote: Vedic oral transmission predates its scripts; later Devanagari: अग्नि Agni, ॐ Om.
survivals: yoga and the word itself
a billion living practitioners
deva → 'divine'; the numerals the world counts with
layers.summary: No tradition has carried its oldest hymns across so much time with so little loss. The Vedic fire god Agni is still worshipped at the dawn of every Hindu wedding — four thousand years after his hymns were composed.

layers.name: The Anatolian Synthesis
layers.attestation: The Hittite archives of Ḫattuša — the largest cuneiform library of the Bronze Age — record a deliberately syncretic state pantheon: Hattic, Hurrian and Mesopotamian gods given ranks and dossiers.
layers.scriptNote: Cuneiform in Hittite hands; hieroglyphic Luwian on the monuments.
survivals: the treaty formula — divine witnesses to international law — that echoes through the Hebrew Bible
Yazılıkaya's rock procession, still standing
layers.summary: The Hittites ran the Bronze Age's most deliberate theology: a pantheon as a civil service, with thousand-year-old Sumerian gods retained in the register alongside their own. When their empire fell, the archive baked hard in the fire that destroyed it — and waited three thousand years to be read.

layers.name: The Ugaritic Tablets
layers.attestation: The Baal Cycle, the Epic of Aqhat and the myth of El's banquet survive on tablets from Ugarit — a single generation before the city burned, preserving the Levantine pantheon whole.
layers.scriptNote: The Ugaritic alphabet — 𐎁 bēt, 𐎍 lāmed — the first alphabet ordered in the order we still use.
survivals: El survives in the very names Israel, Ishmael, Samuel
Baal became the byword for false gods — fame by infamy
the divine council scene the Hebrew Bible shares with Ugarit
layers.summary: Ugarit gave us the alphabet's ordering and the storm-god's biography in the same library. Baal's battle with Prince Sea is the Canaanite answer to the question every coast asks: who holds back the water?

layers.name: The Alphabet's Merchants
layers.attestation: Continues Canaanite religion westward: Tyre, Sidon, and Carthage, attested in inscriptions, sacrifice lists and hostile Roman testimony from the Tophet to the sack of Carthage.
layers.region: Levantine coast, then the whole Mediterranean
layers.scriptNote: The Phoenician consonantal alphabet — the direct ancestor of Greek, Latin, and every alphabet on this page.
survivals: every letter you are reading
Carthage's three wars with Rome — mythology as geopolitics
Astarte → Aphrodite across the Aegean
layers.summary: The Phoenicians' great export was not cedar or glass but the alphabet itself — twenty-two letters that unshipped the priestly monopoly on reading and let writing travel in merchant hulls.

layers.name: The Choice
layers.attestation: Zarathustra's date is honestly uncertain (mainstream c. 1000–600 BCE; traditional c. 1500 BCE). The Gāthās are the oldest confidently datable religious poetry after the Rigveda, and the faith still keeps its sacred fire.
layers.scriptNote: Avestan scripture, fixed in a purpose-built alphabet in Sasanian times: 𐬀𐬵𐬎𐬭𐬀 Ahura.
survivals: the moral engine of the modern world — good against evil, choice as cosmology
the magi at Bethlehem; Nowruz on the spring equinox
fire temples still burning in Yazd
layers.summary: Zarathustra inverted the old order: the gods were not to be bribed but obeyed, and history itself became a battleground of truth against the lie. Every subsequent faith of the single God inherits the question he asked.

layers.name: The Canon
layers.attestation: Zeus, Poseidon and Dionysos appear in Linear B tablets at Knossos and Pylos — the Greek gods are older than the Greek alphabet. Homer and Hesiod fixed the canon around 750–700 BCE.
layers.region: The Aegean, then the Mediterranean world
layers.scriptNote: Linear B → the Greek alphabet: ΑΘΗΝΑ, ΔΙΟΣ — the vowels, the first true alphabet.
survivals: the planets' names
every drama, ode, myth and muse in the Western vocabulary
the word 'panic', the word 'music', the word 'chaos'
layers.summary: Greece did not invent the gods — it invented the argument about them. Hesiod's Theogony is the first attempt anywhere to file the divine world in order, and Athens staged the gods as literature for a paying public.

layers.name: The Adoption
layers.attestation: Rome kept its own numina and household gods, then adopted Greece's pantheon wholesale — by interpretatio romana, every foreign god found a Roman desk.
layers.scriptNote: The Latin alphabet — Rome's most durable province is the alphabet itself.
survivals: the calendar's months and the week's days in Latin Europe
the planet names through Rome's forms
a third of English, and all of law's vocabulary
layers.summary: Rome's genius was administrative, and its theology shows it: it ran a pantheon the way it ran a province — absorb, rename, standardize, endure. The gods of conquered Gaul, Britain and Syria all ended up keeping Rome's books.

layers.name: The Island Memory
layers.eraLabel: La Tène (c. 450 BCE) — recorded c. 8th–12th century CE
layers.attestation: The continental Celts left no scripture; the tradition survives through medieval Irish and Welsh manuscripts copying oral matter far older than their inks — the oldest vernacular literature north of the Alps.
layers.scriptNote: Ogham on the stones (ᚠᚢᚏᚐᚉᚔᚔᚅᚔᚐ); Latin script for the manuscripts.
survivals: Samhain → Halloween
the Matter of Britain — Arthur and his court
the Otherworld, still stock imagery of fantasy
layers.summary: The Celts trusted memory over inscription, and nearly paid the ultimate price for it: Rome destroyed the druids' schools, and the tradition survived only where Rome never ruled — Ireland's monks, writing out of sheer love of the matter.

layers.name: The Eddic Record
layers.eraLabel: Proto-Germanic roots (c. 500 BCE); recorded c. 1200 CE
layers.attestation: The gods' names run in runes from the earliest Germanic inscriptions; the myths themselves were fixed in Iceland's Eddas only after most of Scandinavia had converted — a rescue mission in manuscript.
layers.scriptNote: The runic rows — ᚦ ᚱ ᛟ — and the Latin letters the sagas were written in.
survivals: Tuesday through Friday are Týr, Óðinn, Þórr and Frigg
Tolkien and Wagner's entire careers
Ragnarök, the template of every end-of-the-world story
layers.summary: The Norse gods were never worshipped in temples of stone — they lived in halls of timber and in the skalds' verses, and they die at Ragnarök knowing it. It is the only major pantheon whose own mythology ends.

layers.name: The Last Pagans of Europe
layers.eraLabel: attested 13th–14th century CE; continuity far older
layers.attestation: Baltic religion is attested almost entirely by hostile chronicles — Peter of Dusburg, the Polish and Teutonic records — because it was still being practised, at scale, when Christian Europe wrote it down to end it. Lithuania was Europe's last great pagan state.
layers.region: The Baltic coast — Lithuania and Latvia
layers.scriptNote: No native writing; the chronicles' Latin is our window, and the living Baltic languages our survivors.
survivals: Lithuanian — the most archaic living Indo-European tongue
thunder-worship folklore across the whole Baltic
Romuva's modern restoration
layers.summary: While cathedrals rose across Europe, the Balts still crowned their kings beneath sacred oaks, and crusades were preached against them. Their religion's source is the enemy's diary — read it against the grain.

layers.name: The Dual Faith
layers.attestation: Procopius names the Slavic gods in the 6th century; medieval chronicles (Kiev, Novgorod, Thietmar of Merseburg) record the cults — and dvoeverie, 'dual faith', kept them alive under Christianity for a thousand years.
layers.scriptNote: Attested through Cyrillic chronicles — Перунъ Perun in the Primary Chronicle.
survivals: Easter and Christmas still carry Kupala and Koliada rites
the byliny epic cycles
Slavic folklore as the nursery of the world's fantasy villains and heroes
layers.summary: The Slavic solution to conversion was not resistance but persistence: the gods withdrew into folklore and came back every festival. Perun's oaths became Perun's curses became, simply, thunder.

layers.name: The Turning of the Wheel
layers.attestation: Siddhartha Gautama's life is dated by modern scholarship to c. 5th century BCE; within five centuries the dharma had walked from the Ganges to the Silk Road to Japan — the fastest long-distance spread of any faith before Islam.
layers.languageFamily: Sanskrit and Pali sources; every Asian script follows
layers.scriptNote: Sanskrit sutras in Devanagari and Siddhaṃ; the dharma wheel itself as emblem.
survivals: half a billion practitioners
the word “mindfulness”
the stupa, reborn as every pagoda from Nepal to Japan
layers.summary: Buddhism's great move was to export not gods but methods — and then, on arrival, to crown bodhisattvas anyway: Avalokiteśvara, Amitābha, the medicine Buddha. Compassion, personified, walked further than any army.

layers.name: The Middle Kingdom's Register
layers.attestation: The Shang kings scratched their questions to the high god Di 帝 into oracle bone — the first Chinese writing and the first Chinese theology arrive together. Three thousand years of continuous record follow.
layers.region: The Yellow River to all of China
layers.scriptNote: Oracle bone → bronze → seal → the characters used today: 天 heaven, 帝 the Lord, 神 spirit.
survivals: the world's oldest continuously used writing system
Lunar New Year, the largest annual human migration
the bureaucracy of heaven mirrored in every dynasty's administration
layers.summary: China's gods were administered as carefully as its provinces: canonized, promoted, merged, and filed. The Jade Emperor's celestial ministry is the longest-running celestial civil service on record.

layers.name: The Way and Its Power
layers.eraLabel: Dàodéjīng c. 4th century BCE; organized religion c. 2nd century CE — present
layers.attestation: The Dàodéjīng is a short text with an endless afterlife; organized Taoism begins with the Way of the Celestial Masters in 142 CE and has kept registers, revelations and immortals ever since.
layers.scriptNote: The Eight Trigrams 乾坤震巽坎離艮兌 — diagram as scripture.
survivals: yin and yang as a global idea
tai chi in every park on Earth
feng shui at every property closing
layers.summary: Taoism alone refused the question. Where other strata ask 'which gods rule?', the Dàodéjīng answers that the Way that can be named is not the eternal Way — and then, gloriously, goes on to name its immortals anyway.

layers.name: The Altar of the Three
layers.eraLabel: Dangun legend (traditional 2333 BCE); attested medieval — present
layers.attestation: The founding myth — Hwanin, Hwanung, the bear-woman, and Dangun — is recorded in medieval chronicles carrying far older oral matter; the mudang shamans never stopped practising it.
layers.scriptNote: Hanja and then Hangul — the alphabet the king invented in 1443 and the shamans adopted at once.
survivals: mudang rituals still performed, UNESCO-listed
the national foundation myth, told in every school
Samshin, the triple goddess of childbirth, still invoked
layers.material: white paper and mountain shrine stone
layers.summary: Korea's tradition kept its shamanic spine through every dynasty: three gods in one, a bear who fasted to become a woman, and a founder who lived a thousand years — half bear, half god, half of everything at once.

layers.name: The Kami's Islands
layers.eraLabel: Kojiki 712 CE, Nihon Shoki 720 CE — present
layers.attestation: Japan's myths were written down late but remember much older practice; Shinto's kami cults were never interrupted — the same shrines, the same festivals, the same imperial rites, continuously.
layers.scriptNote: Man'yōgana → kana; the sun goddess's name in the oldest script we have: 天照 Amaterasu.
survivals: Ise Jingū, rebuilt every twenty years since 690 CE
the torii as the world's most recognized gate
matsuri festival life in every neighbourhood
layers.summary: Amaterasu's grandson descended to rule Japan, and the imperial line has claimed descent ever since — the only living monarchy on Earth with a goddess for a founder. The mirror that lured her from the cave is one of the Three Treasures of the throne.

layers.name: The Triangle of the Sea
layers.eraLabel: settlement c. 1000 BCE–1200 CE; continuity unbroken
layers.attestation: The greatest navigation story ever told — settling a triangle of ocean larger than every continent combined — carried its pantheon by memory across open water: Hawaii to Rapa Nui to Aotearoa, all one star-map.
layers.scriptNote: No writing until contact — the geneaologies were chanted, syllable by syllable, canoe by canoe.
survivals: the wayfinding renaissance — voyaging canoes sailing the old routes today
tatau — the tattooing that gave the world the word
hula, oli, and the chant forms that carried the gods
layers.summary: Every other stratum spread by land or by conquest; this one spread by dead reckoning at night. Tangaroa's ocean, Māui's hooks, Pele's volcanoes — a pantheon compact enough to carry in a canoe and strong enough to hold a tenth of the planet's water.

layers.name: The Fifth Sun
layers.eraLabel: c. 1300–1521 CE (Mexica), on Toltec and Teotihuacan roots centuries older
layers.attestation: The Mexica state kept its gods in books — the Borgia, Fejérváry-Mayer and Florentine Codices — and in a temple rebuilt five times at the heart of Tenochtitlan, excavated today under Mexico City's cathedral.
layers.scriptNote: Aztec pictorial codices; Nahuatl in Latin letters after 1521 saved the poetry.
survivals: chocolate, tomato, avocado, coyote, ocelot — the world's Nahuatl loanwords
Día de los Muertos, layers deep in Nahua practice
the Sun Stone on every wall of Mexico
layers.summary: The Mexica believed the fifth world-sun would die by earthquake unless it was fed — and fed it with the one currency that moves the sun: human hearts. The theology was precise, the mathematics superb, and the covenant terrible.

layers.name: Children of the Sun
layers.eraLabel: Inca state c. 1438–1533 CE; Andean roots to Chavín (c. 900 BCE)
layers.attestation: The Andes stacked three thousand years of cult before the Inca: Chavín, Tiwanaku, Wari. The Inca wove them into a state religion — Inti the sun, Viracocha the creator, the huacas of every ridge and river — and administered it province by province.
layers.scriptNote: No alphabet — the khipu knotted cords kept the empire's accounts and, perhaps, its prayers.
survivals: eight million Quechua speakers and rising
Inti Raymi, the sun festival, restored and growing every June
the potato — domesticated here — feeding half the world
layers.summary: The Inca built without wheels, mortar, or writing — and ran an empire of ten million with knotted string. Their gods were the mountains themselves, and the mountains are still there.

layers.name: The Orisha Across the Water
layers.eraLabel: Ife florescence c. 11th–15th century CE; practice unbroken — present
layers.attestation: Ife's naturalistic bronzes and the Ifá divination corpus anchor the tradition archaeologically; the transatlantic slave trade carried it to the Americas, where it never stopped — Candomblé, Santería, Trinidadian Orisha.
layers.region: Yorubaland — Nigeria and Benin; the Atlantic diaspora
layers.scriptNote: Ifá divination patterns — the binary odù corpus — read and recited by babalawo to this day.
survivals: the orisha cults alive across the Americas — the most successful survival of any tradition across the Middle Passage
Afrobeat's spiritual spine
the cities of Ife and Ile-Ife, still sacred ground
layers.summary: No tradition on Earth survived a greater crime with greater power. Carried across the ocean in the minds of the enslaved, the orisha took root in new soil and grew back across the water — Shango's thunder heard in Havana, Bahia and Brooklyn alike.

layers.name: The People of the Land
layers.eraLabel: attested c. 16th century CE; continuity unbroken — present
layers.attestation: Spanish chronicles record the Mapuche cosmos — Pillán the thunder spirits of the volcanoes, Ngen the lords of place, the silver branch — while the machi shamans carried the tradition undefeated through war, mission and dictatorship.
layers.scriptNote: An oral tradition; the machi's rewe — the steps-and-ladder shamanic pole — is its diagram.
survivals: We Tripantu, the Mapuche new year, openly celebrated again
machis — women-led shamanic tradition — practising now
the only indigenous army to stop the Spanish Empire's expansion in open war
layers.summary: The Mapuche held the Araucanía for three centuries against the empire that conquered the Inca and the Aztec — and their religion held with them: a covenant with the land itself, where every river and ridge has its Ngen, and the machi climbs her rewe between worlds.

layers.name: When the Land Became Myth
layers.attestation: The youngest stratum is not a people but a move: Greece personified its own geography — Asia, Europe, Atlantis, the rivers and cities as beings — and the map itself joined the pantheon.
layers.scriptNote: Ἀσία, Ἀτλαντίς, Ὄλυμπος — place-names carrying their stories like epithets.
survivals: every continent's name is a mythological being
Atlas holding up the world's maps — and its astronomy
the Atlantis industry, three thousand years of speculation
layers.summary: The final stratum before the surface: the moment myth annexed geography. Asia was a nymph, Europa a bull-riding queen, Atlantis a cautionary fever-dream — and we still live on the map they made. This is where PuniCodex's own work begins: the names, kept alive.
